question: Should ClickClack realtime websocket frames fail at a hard 1 MiB cap on upgrade, replacing ws's 100 MiB default?
rationale: The patch is a useful security hardening, but it intentionally changes the accepted frame-size contract for existing ClickClack deployments and the event payload type remains open-ended in code.

options.title: Accept 1 MiB Cap
options.body: Land as-is if maintainers consider ClickClack realtime events contractually small id/cursor JSON envelopes and prefer bounded failure for oversized frames.

options.title: Raise Or Document Cap
options.body: Ask for a larger shared cap or explicit ClickClack service-contract documentation if legitimate realtime events can exceed 1 MiB.

options.title: Pause For Service Contract
options.body: Hold the PR until the ClickClack server-side event envelope limit is confirmed.

recommendation.title: Accept 1 MiB Cap
recommendation.body: Land as-is if maintainers consider ClickClack realtime events contractually small id/cursor JSON envelopes and prefer bounded failure for oversized frames.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior merged ClickClack response-size hardening and adjacent tests make this the closest recent history for the cap-size decision.
